assertion: More than 2.1 million acres burned across the state this year, according to the Oregon Department of Forestry, surpassing the previous record set in 2024.
sql: SELECT fire_year, SUM(COALESCE(gis_acres, incident_size_acres)) FROM disasters.wildfire_perimeters WHERE state_fips='41' AND incident_type_category='WF' GROUP BY fire_year
independent_value: OPB Sept. 1 report: 2.5M acres as of Aug. 20
reason: Record direction confirmed; magnitude understated relative to other sources.

assertion: about 13% more than the previous record of 1.9 million acres set in 2024.
sql: SELECT fire_year, SUM(COALESCE(gis_acres, incident_size_acres)) FROM disasters.wildfire_perimeters WHERE state_fips='41' AND incident_type_category='WF' AND fire_year IN (2024,2026) GROUP BY fire_year
reason: Inconsistent with own outlet's earlier figure and the arithmetic.

assertion: More than half the total acres burned in Oregon can be attributed to just five wildfires.
sql: SELECT incident_name, COALESCE(gis_acres, incident_size_acres) FROM disasters.wildfire_perimeters WHERE state_fips='41' AND fire_year=2026 AND incident_type_category='WF' ORDER BY 2 DESC FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

assertion: firefighting costs passed $235 million by mid-August, exceeding the final net costs of the record-setting 2024 fire season by roughly $35 million.
independent_value: $236.2M as of Aug. 20; +$35.3M vs 2024 final net
reason: Matches; date is Aug. 20 not strictly mid-August; partial-season figure.

assertion: By late August, state officials projected total wildfire costs could climb to $350 million. The Oregon Legislature's Joint Emergency Board approved $123 million in additional wildfire funding, including $108 million for the state forestry department and $15 million for the state fire marshal. ODF plans to borrow $150 million under House Bill 3940.
measure: Oregon Legislature Emergency Board wildfire funding forestry department
why_not: The fetched Sept. 1 OPB page matches only the $150M HB 3940 borrowing; the $350M projection and the $123M/$108M/$15M Joint Emergency Board allocations do not appear in it (the '$15' hit is within '$150 million'), so the grade is unchanged.

assertion: The number of Oregonians under evacuation notices peaked on July 27, when 18,193 people were under Level 1, 8,077 under Level 2 and 6,344 under Level 3 orders; the average number of reported wildfires since 2022 was around 2,100 and 1,813 fires were reported in 2026.
measure: Oregon wildfire evacuation notices Level 1 2 3 people
reason: ODEM and ODF pages returned no usable data (evacuation page blank); warehouse holds perimeters only (488 in 2026). OPB Sept. 1 said more than 1,500 fires by Aug. 20, consistent.

assertion: Last winter, Oregon's statewide snowpack sat at a record low, nearly 30% below the previous record set in 2015.
independent_value: Feb. 2026 statewide SWE 2.9 in., nearly 30% below 2015
reason: February snapshot; later USDA reports confirm record low.

assertion: Farmers in 18 Oregon counties are eligible for the U.S. Department of Agriculture Farm Service Agency emergency loans.
independent_value: FSA release: 9 primary + 15 contiguous = 24 counties; deadline Sept. 30, 2027 correct
reason: County count not supported; designation trigger is storms/flooding with drought criteria, not wildfire.

assertion: Gov. Tina Kotek ordered all flags at Oregon public institutions to be lowered in honor of both men killed.
independent_value: KVAL reports Kotek ordered flags lowered for Gutierrez Toral (Sept. 22); no support found for a single order covering both men
reason: Only the Gutierrez Toral tribute was confirmed; Ensign tribute not verified. Deaths of Ensign (dozer, Wrights Spring Fire) and Gutierrez Toral (age 25, Austin Fire) confirmed.

assertion: Another low-snowpack year could raise the risk of drought in 2027, said Larry O'Neill, Oregon's state climatologist.
speaker: Larry O'Neill
independent_value: OPB Sept. 7: 'Another season with low snowpack could set the stage for drought in 2027'; most precipitation expected as rain
